summary:
Solaris is an interactive, web-based simulation designed to tackle the extreme operational challenges of lunar exploration at the Moon's South Pole. Built using standard web technologies, the system integrates a central Mission Control hub with three specialized educational mini-games that focus on critical survival tasks: stratospheric ice drilling, thermodynamic water purification, and low-angle solar array alignment.

The primary objective of the platform is to translate complex aerospace engineering and planetary science into hands-on, problem-solving gameplay. By forcing players to carefully balance finite resources—such as water extraction, power generation, and equipment protection against harsh environmental hazards—the system mirrors the real-world trade-offs faced during Artemis-style lunar missions.

Ultimately, Solaris serves as an accessible educational tool that builds procedural resilience, spatial reasoning, and technical understanding. It provides students, educators, and space enthusiasts with a lightweight, browser-ready way to experience the logistical complexities of sustainable deep-space habitation.
details:
Project Details

What the Project Does: Solaris is an interactive, web-based lunar exploration simulation designed to tackle the extreme operational challenges of the Moon's South Pole at Shackleton Crater. The system immerses users in a Mission Control hub (index.html) where they coordinate three specialized educational subsystems and mini-games: a cryo-stratigraphy ice drill puzzle (extracting frozen core samples), a thermodynamic water purification pipeline (refining harvested ice into pure station water), and an azimuthal solar array memory-matching game (angling photovoltaic towers toward grazing horizon sunlight).

How It Works & Technology Used: Built as a lightweight, browser-ready application using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, and JSON data structures, Solaris runs smoothly across modern devices without requiring external game engines or heavy installations. The development process was powered by VSCode alongside AI assistance from Gemini and ChatGPT, while visual and audio assets were curated using Flaticons, ElevenLabs, and HeyGen. Players navigate through the main dashboard to trigger interactive puzzles that dynamically update resource metrics, and state feedback loops.

Project Creativity & Scientific Grounding: The project creatively transforms complex STEM concepts—such as low-angle horizon sunlight, vacuum thermodynamics, and regolith stratification—into tactile, problem-solving gameplay rather than passive reading. By bridging authentic aerospace science with engaging mechanics, Solaris simulates the real-world trade-offs of deep-space operations.

Key Benefits & Considerations: The system is designed to foster critical thinking, spatial reasoning, and operational resilience. The team carefully considered user experience, UI fluidity (using custom animations), modular scalability for adding future mission scenarios, and scientific accuracy to ensure students and space enthusiasts gain a realistic understanding of sustainable lunar habitation.
